message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to buy my siblings gifts because they refused to do a Secret Santa this year. Let me break this down step by step. First, I have a bunch of siblings, all grown adults. Every year, buying gifts for everyone, including parents, partners, and kids, has gotten out of control. I'm financially okay, but I just can't afford it this year. My parents also can't afford it, and last year, my mom was really stressed and even depressed trying to buy everyone something. That's not good. Last year, after some resistance, we agreed to do a Secret Santa, and it went pretty well. Or so I thought. This year, one of my siblings threw a fit about doing it. She said she doesn't like "putting rules on holidays" and that it's not fair. As a side note, she and our younger siblings rarely buy anything for anyone. Last year was the first time everyone brought something. Another sibling, who is hosting Christmas, sided with her and said that we won't do a Secret Santa but that you don't have to bring gifts if you don't want to. I'm a man, and I'm wondering if it's okay if I don't buy my siblings gifts this year. I love my family, but I can't afford it. I was planning to get gifts for my nieces and nephews but that's it. So, is it right or wrong for me not to buy gifts for my siblings because they refused to do Secret Santa? Let me think about the pros and cons. On the one hand, Secret Santa was working well last year, and it helped reduce the financial burden. It also made sure that everyone contributed something, which was a good change from previous years where some siblings didn't buy anything. This year, one sibling is refusing to do it, and another is supporting her, which complicates things. On the other hand, I'm struggling financially, and buying gifts for everyone is not feasible. I don't want to end up stressed or in a bad financial situation, especially after seeing how it affected my mom last year. I also need to consider the feelings of my siblings. The one who doesn't like Secret Santa might feel that it's taking away from the holiday spirit, but she and others rarely contribute gifts otherwise. It's a bit hypocritical if she expects others to buy gifts but isn't willing to do so herself. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe instead of Secret Santa, we could agree on a spending limit or a different way to exchange gifts that's more manageable financially. Or perhaps focus on non-material ways to celebrate, like spending quality time together, which might be more meaningful. But if the majority of my siblings, especially the ones who usually don't contribute, are against Secret Santa, it might be hard to enforce. I don't want to be the one causing conflict, but I also can't afford to buy gifts for everyone. I also need to think about how my nieces and nephews feel. I was planning to get them gifts, and I don't want them to feel left out. Maybe I can still get them something small, even if I don't get gifts for my siblings. In the end, I have to prioritize my own financial health and well-being. If buying gifts for my siblings is causing me stress and financial strain, it might be better to step back and focus on what I can afford. I can communicate my situation to them, explaining that I can't afford gifts this year but still want to be part of the celebration in other ways. I also need to consider the long-term effects. If I keep buying gifts every year, it might lead to more stress and possibly burnout. It's important to set boundaries to maintain a healthy relationship with my family. So, after all this thinking, I believe it's okay for me not to buy gifts for my siblings this year if I can't afford it. It's more important to take care of my financial health and find other ways to celebrate the holidays meaningfully without the pressure of gift-giving.
